name: Slovenia
summary: Descendants, the spouse and partners are guaranteed half of their intestate share, other close relatives a third. A foreign resident can choose the law of their nationality (EU Succession Regulation art. 22). Slovenia has no trusts; foundation law was not confirmed for private use.
reserved_share: Necessary heirs: descendants, adopted children, parents, spouse and partners; grandparents and siblings only if permanently unable to work and without means (Inheritance Act, ZD, art. 25). Share per art. 26: descendants and spouse one half of the intestate share, others one third (figures from the statute as known, not stated on e-Justice).
foreign_law_note: EU Succession Regulation: the law of the last habitual residence applies by default (art. 21), but a resident foreign national may choose the law of their nationality (art. 22).
trust_note: Slovenia is not in the HCCH table for the 1985 Trusts Convention. Slovenian law has no trust. Foundations (ustanove) are governed by the Institutes Act; their private-benefit use was not researched.
open_questions: The 1/2 and 1/3 shares (ZD art. 26) were not confirmed from a source and should be verified.
The foundation statute (Zakon o ustanovah) and whether private-benefit foundations are possible were not sourced.
Special rules for permanently incapable descendants not captured.
